units.zh: 卷八十 宣元六王傳第五十
units.en: Volume 80: Biographies of the Six Princes of Emperors Xuan and Yuan (no. 50).
units.literal: Volume 80: Biographies of the Six Princes of Emperors Xuan and Yuan, Number 50.

units.zh: 孝宣皇帝五男
units.en: Emperor Xuan had five sons.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons.

units.zh: 孝宣皇帝五男。
units.en: Emperor Xuan had five sons.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons.

units.zh: 許皇后生孝元帝，張婕妤生淮陽憲王欽，衛婕妤生楚孝王囂，公孫婕妤生東平思王宇，戎婕妤生中山哀王竟。
units.en: Empress Xu gave birth to Emperor Yuan. Lady Zhang the Honored Lady bore Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin; Lady Wei the Honored Lady bore Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao; Lady Gongsun the Honored Lady bore Prince Si of Dongping, Yu; and Lady Rong the Honored Lady bore Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing.
units.literal: Empress Xu bore Emperor Xiaoyuan; Lady Zhang Jieyu bore Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin; Lady Wei Jieyu bore Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao; Lady Gongsun Jieyu bore Prince Si of Dongping, Yu; Lady Rong Jieyu bore Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing.

units.zh: 淮陽憲王欽
units.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin
units.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin

units.zh: 淮陽憲王欽，元康三年立，母張婕妤有寵於宣帝。
units.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin, was established in the third year of Yuankang (63 BCE). His mother, Lady Zhang the Honored Lady, enjoyed Emperor Xuan’s favor.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin was enfeoffed in the third year of Yuankang; his mother Lady Zhang Jieyu was favored by Emperor Xuan.

units.zh: 霍皇后廢後，上欲立張婕妤為后。
units.en: After Empress Huo was cast aside, the emperor meant to raise Lady Zhang to empress.
units.literal: After Empress Huo was deposed, the emperor wished to make Lady Zhang Jieyu empress.

units.zh: 久之，懲艾霍氏欲害皇太子，乃更選後宮無子而謹慎者，乃立長陵王婕妤為后，令母養太子。
units.en: In time, mindful of how the Huo family had tried to harm the crown prince, he looked elsewhere among his childless, cautious consorts and made Lady Wang of Changling empress, charging her with raising the heir.
units.literal: After a long time, chastened by the Huo clan’s attempt to harm the heir apparent, he instead chose from the rear palace a woman who had borne no sons and was careful and modest, and established Lady Wang Jieyu of Changling as empress, ordering her to mother the heir.

units.zh: 後無寵，希御見，唯張婕妤最幸。
units.en: The new empress soon lost his attention and seldom saw him; Lady Zhang alone remained his favorite.
units.literal: Afterward she had no favor and rarely attended him; only Lady Zhang Jieyu was most favored.

units.zh: 而憲王壯大，好經書、法律，聰達有材，帝甚愛之。
units.en: As the Prince of Huaiyang came of age, he took to the classics and law, proved quick and capable, and won the emperor’s deep affection.
units.literal: The Prince Xian grew to adulthood, loved the classics and statutes, was intelligent and talented, and the emperor loved him greatly.

units.zh: 太子寬仁，喜儒術，上數嗟歎憲王，輔曰：「真我子也！」
units.en: The crown prince was mild and humane and loved Confucian scholarship; the emperor would sigh over Prince Xian and tell his attendants, “Now that is my son!”
units.literal: The heir apparent was generous and humane and delighted in Confucian learning; the emperor often sighed in admiration of the Prince Xian, saying, “He is truly my son!”

units.zh: 常有意欲立張婕妤與憲王，然用太子起於微細，上少依倚許氏，及即位而許后以殺死，太子蚤失母，故弗忍也。
units.en: He often toyed with making Lady Zhang and the prince his succession, yet the crown prince had come up from nothing: as a young man the emperor had leaned on the Xu clan, and after his accession Empress Xu had been executed, leaving the boy motherless—so he could not bring himself to replace him.
units.literal: He often had the intention of establishing Lady Zhang Jieyu and the Prince Xian, but because the heir had risen from low beginnings, in youth he had relied on the Xu family, and when he took the throne Empress Xu had died by execution, and the heir had early lost his mother, therefore he could not bear it.

units.zh: 久之，上以故丞相韋賢子玄成陽狂讓侯兄，經明行高，稱於朝廷，乃召拜玄成為淮陽中尉，欲感諭憲王，輔以推讓之臣，由是太子遂安。
units.en: Years later he recalled how Wei Xuancheng, son of the former chancellor Wei Xian, had played mad to yield his noble title to an elder brother—learned in the classics and renowned for integrity—and summoned him to serve as commandant in Huaiyang, hoping such an example of deference would steady the ambitious prince and quiet the succession.
units.literal: After a long time, because the former Chancellor Wei Xian’s son Xuancheng feigned madness to yield the marquisate to his elder brother, was clear in the classics and high in conduct, and was praised at court, he summoned and appointed Xuancheng as Commandant of Huaiyang, wishing to instruct and admonish the Prince Xian and support him with a minister who practiced yielding; thereby the heir apparent was secured.

units.zh: 宣帝崩，元帝即位，乃遣憲王之國。
units.en: When Xuan died and Yuan ascended, the new emperor sent Prince Qin to his fief at Huaiyang.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan took the throne, he then sent the Prince Xian to his kingdom.

units.zh: 時，張婕妤已卒，憲王有外祖母，舅張博兄弟三人歲至淮陽見親，輒受王賜。
units.en: By then Lady Zhang was dead. The prince still had kin on his mother’s side: each year his uncles Zhang Bo and his two brothers visited Huaiyang and went home laden with the king’s largesse.
units.literal: At that time Lady Zhang Jieyu had already died; the Prince Xian had a maternal grandmother, and his uncles Zhang Bo and his two brothers each year came to Huaiyang to visit kin and received gifts from the king.

units.zh: 後王上書，請徙外家張氏於國。
units.en: Later the prince petitioned to bring his mother’s Zhang relatives to live in his state.
units.literal: Later the king submitted a memorial asking to move his maternal Zhang kin into the kingdom.

units.zh: 博上書，願留守墳墓，獨不徙。
units.en: Bo memorialized that he wished to stay behind to tend the family graves and not relocate.
units.literal: Bo submitted a memorial wishing to remain to guard the tombs alone and not move.

units.zh: 王恨之。
units.en: The prince nursed a grudge against him.
units.literal: The king resented him.

units.zh: 後博至淮陽，王賜之少。
units.en: When Bo next arrived in Huaiyang, the king’s gifts were stingy.
units.literal: Later when Bo came to Huaiyang, the king gave him little.

units.zh: 博言：「負責數百萬，願王為償。」
units.en: Bo said, “I am several million cash in debt; I need the king to cover it.”
units.literal: Bo said, “I owe several million in debt; I wish the king would repay it for me.”

units.zh: 王不許，博辭去，令弟光恐云王遇大人益解，博欲上書為大人乞骸骨去。
units.en: The king refused. As Bo left, he had his younger brother Guang alarm the prince, saying that the king was growing cold toward the elder and that Bo meant to memorialize asking leave for the elder to retire.
units.literal: The king did not permit it. Bo departed and had his younger brother Guang frighten the king, saying the king’s treatment of the elder was growing colder and that Bo wished to submit a memorial asking that the elder be allowed to retire.

units.zh: 王乃遣人持黃金五十斤送博。
units.en: The prince then dispatched an agent with fifty jin of gold for Bo.
units.literal: The king then sent a man with fifty jin of gold to deliver to Bo.

units.zh: 博喜，還書謝，為諂語盛稱譽王，因言：「當今朝廷無賢臣，災變數見，足為寒心。
units.en: Bo was delighted and wrote back in fulsome praise, saying, “The court today is bereft of good men; portents and disasters pile up—it is enough to freeze one’s blood.
units.literal: Bo was pleased and returned a letter of thanks with flattering words that greatly praised the king, saying, “At present the court has no worthy ministers; disasters and anomalies appear repeatedly—enough to chill the heart.

units.zh: 萬姓咸歸望於大王，大王奈何恬然不求入朝見，輔助主上乎？」
units.en: The people are looking to you, my lord—how can you sit idle and not press for an audience to steady the throne?”
units.literal: The myriad common people all turn their hopes to the great king; how can the great king remain indifferent and not seek to enter court and assist the lord above?”

units.zh: 使弟光數說王宜聽博計，令於京師說用事貴人為王求朝。
units.en: He had his younger brother Guang repeatedly urge the king to listen to Bo’s plan, and had Bo speak in the capital to powerful nobles who handled affairs, seeking an audience for the king.
units.literal: He had his younger brother Guang repeatedly urge the king that he ought to follow Bo’s plan and have him speak to powerful men at the capital who handle affairs to seek an audience for the king.

units.zh: 許不納其言。
units.en: The prince would not heed him.
units.literal: His words were not accepted.

units.zh: 後光欲至長安，辭王，復言「願盡力與博共為王求朝。
units.en: When Guang later prepared to leave for Chang’an, he again assured the king, “Bo and I will do everything we can to win you a summons.
units.literal: Later Guang wished to go to Chang’an, took leave of the king, and again said, “I wish to exert myself together with Bo to seek an audience for the king.

units.zh: 王即日至長安，可因平陽侯。」
units.en: Once you reach Chang'an, the Marquis of Pingyang can open the door for you.”
units.literal: If the king arrives in Chang’an the same day, you may do so through the Marquis of Pingyang.”

units.zh: 光得王欲求朝語，馳使人語博。
units.en: Guang carried the prince’s agreement to Bo by fast courier.
units.literal: Guang obtained the king’s words desiring an audience and galloped a messenger to tell Bo.

units.zh: 博知王意動，復遺王書曰：「博幸得肺腑，數進愚策，未見省察。
units.en: Bo saw the hook take and wrote again: “I have presumed on our kinship and offered counsel again and again, yet you have never truly weighed it.
units.literal: Bo knew the king’s mind was moved and again sent the king a letter saying, “Bo has fortunately been as close as lungs and liver, several times advancing foolish plans without having been examined.

units.zh: 北遊燕、趙，欲循行郡國求幽隱之士，聞齊有駟先生者，善為《司馬兵法》，大將之材也，博得謁見，承間進問五帝、三王究竟要道，卓爾非世俗之所知。
units.en: I have ridden through Yan and Zhao seeking hidden worthies and learned of Master Si in Qi, master of the Sima fa—true material for a grand captain. I gained an audience and, when the moment allowed, pressed him on the deepest doctrine of the Five Emperors and Three Kings—insights this world seldom hears.
units.literal: I traveled north through Yan and Zhao, wishing to tour the commanderies and kingdoms seeking reclusive gentlemen; I heard that in Qi there is Master Si who is good at the Sima fa on war—material for a great general—and Bo was able to meet him and, taking an opening, advanced questions on the essential way of the Five Emperors and Three Kings—outstanding, not what the vulgar know.

units.zh: 今邊境不安，天下騷動，微此人其莫能安也。
units.en: The frontier is unquiet and the empire roiled; without such a man there may be no peace.
units.literal: Now the borders are not secure and the realm is in turmoil; without this man perhaps none can bring peace.

units.zh: 又聞北海之瀕有賢人焉，累世不可逮，然難致也。
units.en: They say another sage lives by the northern sea, unequalled for generations though nearly impossible to draw out.
units.literal: I also heard that on the shore of the Northern Sea there is a worthy man, generations cannot match him, yet he is hard to summon.

units.zh: 得此二人而薦之，功亦不細矣。
units.en: To present both to the throne would be no small service.
units.literal: To obtain these two men and recommend them would also be no small achievement.

units.zh: 博願馳西以此赴助漢急，無財幣以通顯之。
units.en: I would ride west tomorrow to serve the dynasty in its straits, but I lack the gold to open the right doors.
units.literal: Bo wishes to gallop west with this to aid the Han in its urgency, but has no wealth or currency to gain access for them.

units.zh: 趙王使謁者持牛、酒，黃金三十斤勞博，博不受；
units.en: The king of Zhao sent wine, oxen, and thirty jin of gold; Bo declined them;
units.literal: The King of Zhao sent his usher with cattle, wine, and thirty jin of gold to reward Bo; Bo did not accept;

units.zh: 復使人願尚女，聘金二百斤，博未許。
units.en: he then offered a daughter in marriage with two hundred jin as bride-price, and Bo still hesitated.
units.literal: again he sent a man wishing to give a daughter in marriage with bride-price of two hundred jin, and Bo had not yet consented.

units.zh: 會得光書云大王已遣光西，與博並力求朝。
units.en: Then your letter arrived, my lord, saying you had sent Guang west to join me in pressing for your audience.
units.literal: Just then he received Guang’s letter saying the great king had already sent Guang west to join Bo in striving together for an audience.

units.zh: 博自以棄捐，不意大王還意反義，結以硃顏，願殺身報德。
units.en: I thought myself forgotten; I never dreamed you would honor me again and bind me with such kindness. I would lay down my life to repay it.
units.literal: Bo considered himself cast aside and did not expect the great king to turn his regard back in righteousness and bind him with crimson countenance; he wishes to kill himself to repay virtue.

units.zh: 朝事何足言！
units.en: The audience itself is the least of it!
units.literal: What is there to say about the matter of an audience!

units.zh: 大王誠賜咳唾，使得盡死，湯、禹所以成大功也。
units.en: If my lord will only breathe a word of consent, I will spend my last breath as Tang and Yu did to build great deeds.
units.literal: If the great king truly grants a cough or spittle so that I may exhaust my death, that is how Tang and Yu accomplished great merit.

units.zh: 駟先生蓄積道術，書無不有，願知大王所好，請得輒上。」
units.en: Master Si’s library holds every text under heaven; tell me your interests and I will lay the right volumes before you at once.”
units.literal: Master Si has stored up the way and techniques; there is no book he does not have; I wish to know what the great king favors, and I ask to be able to present it at once.”

units.zh: 王得書喜說，報博書曰：「子高乃幸左顧存恤，發心惻隱，顯至誠，納以嘉謀，語以至事，雖亦不敏，敢不諭意！
units.en: The prince was delighted and answered: “Zi Gao, you have turned back to pity and care for me, spoken from the heart, offered wise counsel and weighty truth—dull though I am, how could I fail to grasp your meaning?
units.literal: The king received the letter and was pleased, and replied to Bo’s letter saying, “Zi Gao has deigned to turn and show care, arousing compassion in the heart, displaying utmost sincerity, accepting fine plans, speaking of the greatest affairs—though I am also not sharp, how dare I fail to understand the intention!

units.zh: 今遣有司為子高償責二百萬。」
units.en: I have ordered my officers to settle your two-million debt this day.”
units.literal: Now I dispatch the responsible officials to repay Zi Gao’s debt of two million.”

units.zh: 是時，博女婿京房以明《易》陰陽得幸於上，數召見言事。
units.en: Bo’s son-in-law Jing Fang had won favor by expounding the Book of Changes and yin–yang theory and was repeatedly called to advise the throne.
units.literal: At this time Bo’s son-in-law Jing Fang, through clarity in the Changes and yin and yang, had gained the emperor’s favor and was several times summoned to speak on affairs.

units.zh: 自謂為石顯、五鹿充宗所排，謀不得用，數為博道之。
units.en: He complained that Shi Xian and Wulu Chongzong had blocked him and that none of his policies were adopted, and he poured this out to Bo again and again.
units.literal: He claimed that he was squeezed out by Shi Xian and Wulu Chongzong and his plans could not be used, and several times spoke of this to Bo.

units.zh: 博常欲誑耀淮陽王，即具記房諸所說災異及召見密語，持予淮陽王以為信驗，詐言：「已見中書令石君求朝，許以金五百斤。
units.en: Bo had long wanted to impress the King of Huaiyang, so he wrote down everything Jing Fang had said about disasters and anomalies, along with confidential remarks from imperial audiences, and brought the notes to the king as proof. He falsely claimed, “I have already gone to Palace Secretary Shi to ask for an audience; he agreed in exchange for five hundred jin of gold.
units.literal: Bo always wished to dazzle the King of Huaiyang, and so fully recorded all that Fang had said about disasters and anomalies and secret words at audiences, and took them to give to the King of Huaiyang as proof, falsely saying, “I have already seen Palace Secretary Shi and sought an audience; he promised it for five hundred jin of gold.

units.zh: 賢聖制事，蓋慮功而不計費。
units.en: The sages weighed outcomes, not price tags.
units.literal: The sages in ordering affairs surely weigh merit and do not reckon expense.

units.zh: 昔禹治鴻水，百姓罷勞，成功既立，萬世賴之。
units.en: When Yu tamed the flood, the people wore themselves to the bone, yet once the work was done, countless ages lived by it.
units.literal: In antiquity Yu controlled the flood waters; the common people were exhausted by toil; when the achievement was established, myriad generations relied on it.

units.zh: 今聞陛下春秋未滿四十，發齒墮落，太子幼弱，佞人用事，陰陽不調，百姓疾疫饑饉死者且半，鴻水之害殆不過此。
units.en: They say you are not yet forty, yet your hair and teeth fail, the heir is a child, favorites run the court, heaven and earth are out of tune, and plague and famine have carried off perhaps half the realm—no less dire than Yu’s deluge.
units.literal: Now I hear that Your Majesty’s years are not yet forty, hair and teeth are falling, the heir is young and weak, crafty men hold power, yin and yang are not in harmony, and among the common people plague and famine have killed nearly half; the harm of the flood waters is perhaps no worse than this.

units.zh: 大王緒欲救世，將比功德，何可以忽？
units.en: You mean to save the age, my lord—set that deed beside a few hundred jin of gold.
units.literal: The great king in succession wishes to save the age; compared with that merit, how can this be neglected?

units.zh: 博已與大儒知道者為大王為便宜奏，陳安危，指災異，大王朝見，先口陳其意而後奏之，上必大說。
units.en: I have lined up learned men to draft a memorial on peril and portent; when you face the throne, speak the heart of it aloud, then hand up the text, and the Son of Heaven will be overjoyed.
units.literal: Bo has already joined with great Confucians who know the way to draft for the great king a convenient memorial stating safety and danger, pointing to disasters and anomalies; when the great king has his audience, first declare the intent orally and then submit it, and the emperor will surely be greatly pleased.

units.zh: 事成功立，大王即有周、邵之名，邪臣散亡，公卿變節，功德亡比，而梁、趙之寵必歸大王，外家亦將富貴，何復望大王之金錢？」
units.en: Success would give you the stature of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, sweep the sycophants from power, and turn every minister’s coat—while the favor now lavished on Liang and Zhao would fall to you and your wife’s clan. Why haggle over gold?”
units.literal: When the affair succeeds and the achievement is established, the great king will then have the names of the dukes of Zhou and Shao, wicked ministers will scatter and flee, dukes and ministers will change their ways, merit without compare—and the favor shown Liang and Zhao will surely return to the great king, and the maternal kin will also become rich and noble; why look again to the great king’s gold and cash?”

units.zh: 王喜說，報博書曰：「乃者詔下，止諸侯朝者，寡人憯然不知所出。
units.en: The prince wrote back gladly: “When the edict lately barred princes from audience, I was at a loss.
units.literal: The king was pleased and replied to Bo’s letter saying, “Recently an edict came down forbidding the feudal kings from attending court; I was dismayed and did not know what to do.

units.zh: 子高素有顏、冉之資，臧武之智，子貢之辯，卞莊子之勇，兼此四者，世之所鮮。
units.en: You have Yan Hui’s and Ran Boniu’s gifts, Zang Wuzhong’s wit, Zigong’s tongue, and Bian Zhuangzi’s nerve—four virtues seldom met in one man.
units.literal: Zi Gao has always had the endowment of Yan and Ran, the wisdom of Zang Wuzhong, the eloquence of Zigong, and the courage of Bian Zhuangzi; to combine these four is rare in the world.

units.zh: 既開端緒，願卒成之。
units.en: You have opened the way; see it through with me.
units.literal: Since the beginning has been opened, I wish to see it through to the end.

units.zh: 求朝，義事也，奈何行金錢乎！」
units.en: Seeking an audience is a matter of right—how can we buy it with money!”
units.literal: To seek an audience is a righteous affair; how can one traffic in gold and cash!”

units.zh: 博報曰：「已許石君，須以成事。」
units.en: Bo answered, “I have given Shi my word—we need the gold to finish this.”
units.literal: Bo replied saying, “I have already promised Secretary Shi; we must use it to complete the affair.”

units.zh: 王以金五百斤予博。
units.en: The prince handed over five hundred jin of gold.
units.literal: The king gave Bo five hundred jin of gold.

units.zh: 會房出為郡守，離左右，顯具有此事告之。
units.en: Then Jing Fang was posted away from court, and Shi Xian laid the whole intrigue before the emperor.
units.literal: Just then Fang went out as governor of a commandery, left the emperor’s side, and Shi Xian fully reported this matter to him.

units.zh: 房漏洩省中語，博兄弟詿誤諸侯王，誹謗政治，狡猾不道，皆下獄。
units.en: Fang had divulged palace secrets; Bo and his brothers had led a prince astray and defamed the state—charges of wicked irreverence—and all were clapped in jail.
units.literal: Fang leaked words from within the palace; Bo and his brothers misled the feudal kings, slandered the government, and were crafty and contrary to the Way; all were cast into prison.

units.zh: 有司奏請逮捕欽，上不忍致法，遣諫大夫王駿賜欽璽書曰：「皇帝問淮陽王。
units.en: Officials asked to arrest Prince Qin; the emperor relented and sent Grandee Remonstrant Wang Jun with a sealed edict: “The Son of Heaven addresses the King of Huaiyang.
units.literal: The responsible officials memorialized requesting Qin’s arrest; the emperor could not bear to apply the law and sent Grandee Remonstrant Wang Jun to bestow on Qin an imperial missive saying, “The emperor inquires of the King of Huaiyang.

units.zh: 有司奏王，王舅張博數遺王書，非毀政治，謗訕天子，褒舉諸侯，稱引周、湯，以諂惑王，所言尤惡，悖逆無道。
units.en: They say your uncle Zhang Bo wrote you again and again, attacking policy, mocking the throne, praising other kings, and invoking the ancient sages only to seduce you—language foul enough to count as treason.
units.literal: The responsible officials have reported on the king: the king’s uncle Zhang Bo several times sent letters to the king, destroying the government, reviling the Son of Heaven, praising the feudal kings, citing Zhou and Tang, thereby flattering and misleading the king; his words were especially vile, rebellious and contrary to the Way.

units.zh: 王不舉奏而多與金錢，報以好言，罪至不赦，朕惻焉不忍聞，為王傷之。
units.en: You never denounced him yet showered him with gold and answered in honeyed words—guilt that admits no pardon. I shrink from hearing it and grieve for you.
units.literal: The king did not report it but gave much gold and cash and replied with fine words; the crime reaches to unpardonable; We are pained and cannot bear to hear it, and We grieve for the king.

units.zh: 推原厥本，不祥自博，惟王之心，匪同於凶。
units.en: Trace the evil to its source and it begins with Bo alone; your own heart was never that of a traitor.
units.literal: Tracing to the root of the origin, ill auspice came from Bo alone; as for the king’s heart, it is not the same as the vicious.

units.zh: 已詔有司勿治王事，遣諫大夫駿申諭朕意。
units.en: I have told my officers not to proceed against you and sent Grandee Remonstrant Jun to make my meaning plain.
units.literal: I have already ordered the responsible officials not to handle the king’s affair, and sent Grandee Remonstrant Jun to declare Our intention.

units.zh: 《詩》不云乎：『靖恭爾位，正直是與』？
units.en: Does not the Classic of Poetry say, “Quiet and reverent in your place; keep company with the upright”?
units.literal: Does not the Odes say, “Be reverent in your station; align with the upright”?

units.zh: 王其勉之！」
units.en: Strive to live by that, my cousin!”
units.literal: Let the king strive in this!”

units.zh: 駿諭指曰：「禮為諸侯制相朝聘之義，蓋以考禮一德，尊事天子也。
units.en: Wang Jun explained: “Ritual sets how kings attend court—to harmonize conduct with the Way and honor the Son of Heaven.
units.literal: Jun declared the meaning saying, “By ritual the feudal kings have regulated the meaning of mutual court visits, in order to examine ritual and unify virtue and honoringly serve the Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 且王不學《詩》乎？
units.en: Have you not read the Odes yourself?
units.literal: Moreover has the king not studied the Odes?

units.zh: 《詩》云：『俾侯於魯，為周室輔。』
units.en: It says, “They made him marquis in Lu, a pillar for the house of Zhou.”
units.literal: The Odes says, “Made marquis in Lu, to be a buttress for the house of Zhou.”

units.zh: 今王舅博數遺王書，所言悖逆。
units.en: Yet your uncle Bo wrote you repeatedly with treasonous counsel.
units.literal: Now the king’s uncle Bo several times sent letters to the king; what he said was rebellious.

units.zh: 王幸受詔策，通經術，知諸侯名譽不當出竟。
units.en: You have received the imperial charge, you know the classics, and you know a king’s name must not cross his borders.
units.literal: The king has fortunately received edicts and orders, comprehends the classics, and knows that a feudal king’s reputation ought not to extend beyond his borders.

units.zh: 天子普覆，德佈於朝，而恬有博言，多予金錢，與相報應，不忠莫大焉。
units.en: The emperor’s grace covers all; his virtue fills the court—yet you swallowed Bo’s plots, paid him in gold, and wrote back as if in league. Nothing is more disloyal.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven’s cover is universal; virtue spreads at court—yet you calmly harbored Bo’s words, gave much gold and cash, and answered in mutual correspondence; no disloyalty is greater.

units.zh: 故事，諸侯王獲罪京師，罪惡輕重，縱不伏誅，必蒙遷削貶黜之罪，未有但已者也。
units.en: By precedent a prince who sins at the capital, whether the fault is great or small, faces exile or stripping of rank if not the axe—never a simple shrug.
units.literal: By precedent, when feudal kings incur guilt at the capital, whether the crime is light or heavy, even if they are not put to death, they surely suffer the punishment of removal, demotion, or dismissal; there has never been a case of stopping there alone.

units.zh: 今聖主赦王之罪，又憐王失計忘本，為博所惑，加賜璽書，使諫大夫申諭至意，殷勤之恩，豈有量哉！
units.en: Yet he forgives you, pities you for forgetting who you are under Bo’s spell, and adds this personal edict and an envoy’s voice—measure that kindness if you can.
units.literal: Now the sage lord has pardoned the king’s crime and also pities the king for losing his bearings and forgetting his roots, being misled by Bo, and has added the gift of an imperial missive and sent a grandee remonstrant to declare the utmost intention—can the depth of this earnest favor be measured?

units.zh: 博等所犯惡大，群下之所共攻，王法之所不赦也。
units.en: Bo’s crimes are monstrous; every minister condemns them and the law cannot spare them.
units.literal: What Bo and the others committed is greatly vile; it is what all below jointly attack and what kingly law does not pardon.

units.zh: 自今以來，王毋復以博等累心，務與眾棄之。
units.en: From this day do not let Bo trouble your thoughts again; join the world in casting him off.
units.literal: From now on, let the king never again let Bo and the others burden his mind; strive together with the multitude to cast them off.

units.zh: 《春秋》之義，大能變改。
units.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that even grave fault may be redeemed by change.
units.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn is that the great can change and reform.

units.zh: 《易》曰『借用白茅，無咎』，言臣子之道，改過自新，潔己以承上，然後免於咎也。
units.en: The Changes speaks of laying white rushes beneath an offering—no blame—meaning a son of the house may cleanse himself, turn anew, and serve his lord without fault.
units.literal: The Changes says, “Borrowing white grass, no blame,” meaning the way of ministers and sons: to reform faults and renew oneself, to purify oneself to receive what is above, and then one escapes blame.

units.zh: 王其留意慎戒，惟思所以悔過易行，塞重責，稱厚恩者。
units.en: Guard your every step; think how to mend your ways, meet this mercy, and silence heavier blame.
units.literal: Let the king take care and be on guard; only think how to repent faults and change conduct, block heavy responsibility, and match thick favor.

units.zh: 如此，則長有富貴，社稷安矣。」
units.en: Do that, and you keep rank and fortune, and the state altars stand firm.”
units.literal: If so, then you will long possess wealth and nobility and the altars of soil and grain will be secure.”

units.zh: 於是淮陽王欽免冠稽首謝曰：「奉籓無狀，過惡暴列，陛下不忍致法，加大恩，遣使者申諭道術守籓之義。
units.en: Prince Qin doffed his cap and kowtowed: “I have disgraced my charge as a bulwark; my crimes lie bare. You would not punish me but sent envoys to teach the duty of a vassal.
units.literal: Thereupon the King of Huaiyang, Qin, removed his cap and knocked his head in thanks saying, “In holding the screen I have lacked deportment; my faults have been exposed in a row; Your Majesty could not bear to apply the law and has extended great favor, dispatching envoys to explain the meaning of the way and of guarding the screen.

units.zh: 伏念博罪惡尤深，當伏重誅。
units.en: Bo’s guilt is the deeper and deserves death.
units.literal: I reflect that Bo’s crime is especially deep and ought to suffer heavy execution.

units.zh: 臣欽願悉心自新，奉承詔策。
units.en: I, Qin, will devote myself anew to obeying your command.
units.literal: Your subject Qin wishes to give his whole heart to renewing himself and to receive and carry out the edicts and orders.

units.zh: 頓首死罪。」
units.en: I kowtow for a crime worthy of death.”
units.literal: I knock my head for the crime deserving death.”

units.zh: 京房及博兄弟三人皆棄市，妻子徙邊。
units.en: Jing Fang and Zhang Bo and his two brothers were executed in the marketplace; their wives and children were banished to the frontier.
units.literal: Jing Fang and Bo and his two brothers were all exposed in the market; wives and children were moved to the border.

units.zh: 至成帝即位，以淮陽王屬為叔父，敬寵之，異於它國。
units.en: When Cheng succeeded, he honored the king of Huaiyang as his father's younger brother, showered favor on him, and treated his domain unlike any other.
units.literal: When Emperor Cheng took the throne, treating the King of Huaiyang as his paternal uncle, he respected and favored him and treated him differently from other kingdoms.

units.zh: 王上書自陳舅張博時事，頗為石顯等所侵，因為博家屬徙者求還。
units.en: The prince memorialized the court about his uncle Zhang Bo, claiming he had been wronged by Shi Xian and his faction, and asked that Bo's banished kin be restored.
units.literal: The king submitted a memorial recounting the affair of his maternal uncle Zhang Bo, that he had been rather encroached upon by Shi Xian and others, and thus asked that the exiled members of Bo's family be allowed to return.

units.zh: 丞相、御史復劾欽：「前與博相遺私書，指意非諸侯王所宜，蒙恩勿治，事在赦前。
units.en: The chancellor and imperial counselor again indicted Qin: "You once exchanged private letters with Bo in ways unbecoming a prince. Though you were spared before the amnesty,
units.literal: The chancellor and imperial counselor again impeached Qin: "Previously you exchanged private letters with Bo; the intent was not appropriate for a feudal king. You received favor and were not prosecuted—the affair occurred before the amnesty.

units.zh: 不悔過而復稱引，自以為直，失籓臣禮，不敬。」
units.en: you now bring it up again without remorse, claiming righteousness. That is a breach of a vassal prince's duty and shows disrespect."
units.literal: Not repenting of your errors, you again cite and refer to it, considering yourself in the right. You have lost the ritual due from a feudal vassal and are disrespectful."

units.zh: 上加恩，許王還徙者。
units.en: The emperor relented and allowed the prince's exiles to come home.
units.literal: The emperor, granting additional favor, permitted the king to have the exiles returned.

units.zh: 三十六年薨。
units.en: He died in the thirty-sixth year of his reign.
units.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died.

units.zh: 子文王玄嗣，二十六年薨。
units.en: His son Prince Wen, Xuan, succeeded and died in the twenty-sixth year of his reign.
units.literal: His son King Wen Xuan succeeded; in the twenty-sixth year he died.

units.zh: 子縯嗣，王莽時絕。
units.en: His son Yan inherited the title; the line ended under Wang Mang.
units.literal: His son Yan succeeded; at the time of Wang Mang the line was cut off.

units.zh: 楚孝王囂，甘露二年立為定陶王，三年徙楚，成帝河平中入朝，時被疾，天子閔之，下詔曰：「蓋聞『天地之性人為貴，人之行莫大於孝』。
units.en: Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao, was enfeoffed as king of Dingtao in Ganlu 2 and transferred to Chu in Ganlu 3. During the He Ping era under Emperor Cheng he came to court but fell ill. The emperor pitied him and issued an edict: "We have heard that 'among the nature of Heaven and Earth, humanity is most prized, and among human conduct nothing is greater than filial piety.'
units.literal: Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao, was established as King of Dingtao in the second year of Ganlu; in the third year he was moved to Chu. Under Emperor Cheng, during the He Ping era, he came to court to pay homage. At that time he was afflicted with illness. The Son of Heaven pitied him and issued an edict, saying: "We have heard that 'among the nature of Heaven and Earth, humanity is most prized, and among human conduct nothing is greater than filial piety.'

units.zh: 楚王囂素行孝順仁慈，之國以來二十餘年，孅介之過未嘗聞，朕甚嘉之。
units.en: King Ao of Chu has always been filial, kind, and humane. In more than twenty years since he took his fief, We have never heard the least fault of him, and We greatly commend him.
units.literal: The King of Chu, Ao, has always acted with filial obedience, kindness, and benevolence. Since coming to his kingdom more than twenty years have passed, and We have never heard of the slightest fault. We greatly commend this.

units.zh: 今乃遭命，離於惡疾，夫子所痛，曰：『蔑之，命矣夫！
units.en: Now fate has struck, and he is stricken with grievous illness. The Master lamented, saying, 'Alas for him! Such is fate!'
units.literal: Now he has encountered fate and is separated by a grievous illness. The Master grieved, saying, 'Alas for him! Such is fate!'

units.zh: 斯人也而有斯疾也！』
units.en: That such a man should have such an illness!
units.literal: That such a man should have such an illness!

units.zh: 朕甚閔焉。
units.en: We are deeply grieved.
units.literal: We are deeply grieved.

units.zh: 夫行純茂而不顯異，則有國者將何勖哉？
units.en: When pure and abundant conduct wins no special recognition, what are rulers to take as encouragement?
units.literal: When conduct is pure and abundant yet no distinction is shown, what shall those who hold states take as encouragement?

units.zh: 《書》不云乎：『用德章厥善』？
units.en: Does not the Documents say, 'With virtue make known his goodness'?
units.literal: Does not the Documents say, 'With virtue make known his goodness'?

units.zh: 今王朝正月，詔與子男一人俱，其以廣戚縣戶四千三百封其子勳為廣戚侯。」
units.en: At this New Year's court audience, let him come with one son. We enfeoff his son Xun with the four thousand three hundred households of Guangqi county as marquis of Guangqi."
units.literal: At this New Year's court audience, let him come with one son or younger brother; We hereby enfeoff his son Xun with four thousand three hundred households of Guangqi county as Marquis of Guangqi."

units.zh: 明年，囂薨。
units.en: The next year Ao died.
units.literal: The next year Ao died.

units.zh: 子懷王文嗣，一年薨，無子，絕。
units.en: His son Prince Huai, Wen, succeeded; he died within a year, leaving no heir, and the line ended.
units.literal: His son King Huai Wen succeeded; in one year he died, without a son, and the line was cut off.

units.zh: 明年，成帝復立文弟平陸侯衍，是為思王。
units.en: The next year Emperor Cheng re-established Wen's younger brother Yan, marquis of Pinglu, as Prince Si.
units.literal: The next year Emperor Cheng again established Wen's younger brother Yan, Marquis of Pinglu, who is known as Prince Si.

units.zh: 二十一年薨，子紆嗣，王莽時絕。
units.en: He died in the twenty-first year of his reign; his son Yu inherited, and the line ended under Wang Mang.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; his son Yu succeeded; at the time of Wang Mang the line was cut off.

units.zh: 初，成帝時又立紆弟景為定陶王。
units.en: Earlier, under Emperor Cheng, Jing—Yu’s younger brother—had been made king of Dingtao.
units.literal: At the beginning, under Emperor Cheng, they again established Jing, younger brother of Yu, as King of Dingtao.

units.zh: 廣戚侯勳薨，謚曰煬侯，子顯嗣。
units.en: The marquis of Guangqi, Xun, died with the posthumous title Yang; his son Xian succeeded.
units.literal: Marquis of Guangqi Xun died; his posthumous title was Marquis Yang; his son Xian succeeded.

units.zh: 平帝崩，無子，王莽立顯子嬰為孺子，奉平帝后。
units.en: When Emperor Ping died childless, Wang Mang set Xian’s son Ying on the throne as the infant heir to carry on Ping’s line.
units.literal: When Emperor Ping died without a son, Wang Mang established Xian’s son Ying as the Infant, to serve Empress Dowager Ping.

units.zh: 莽篡位，以嬰為定安公。
units.en: When Mang seized the throne he demoted Ying to duke of Ding’an.
units.literal: When Mang usurped the throne, he made Ying Duke of Ding’an.

units.zh: 漢既誅莽，更始時嬰在長安，平陵方望等頗知天文，以為更始必敗，嬰本統當立者也，共起兵將嬰至臨涇，立為天子。
units.en: After Han destroyed Wang Mang, Ying was still in Chang’an under the Gengshi regime. Fang Wang of Pingling and others, versed in the stars, believed Gengshi would fall and that Ying was the rightful heir; they rose in arms, escorted him to Linjing, and proclaimed him emperor.
units.literal: When Han had executed Mang, at the time of Gengshi Ying was in Chang’an; Fang Wang and others at Pingling, who knew astronomy somewhat, thought Gengshi would surely fail and that Ying by original succession ought to have been established; they jointly raised troops and brought Ying to Linjing and established him as Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 更始遣丞相李松擊破殺嬰云。
units.en: Gengshi’s chancellor Li Song crushed the rising and killed Ying, or so the record runs.
units.literal: Gengshi sent Chancellor Li Song to attack, defeat, and kill Ying, it is said.

units.zh: 東平思王宇
units.en: Prince Si of Dongping, Yu
units.literal: Prince Si of Dongping, Yu

units.zh: 東平思王宇，甘露二年立。
units.en: Prince Si of Dongping, Yu, was enfeoffed in the second year of Ganlu (52 BCE).
units.literal: Prince Si of Dongping, Yu was established in the second year of Ganlu.

units.zh: 元帝即位，就國。
units.en: When Yuan became emperor, Yu proceeded to his fief.
units.literal: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, he went to his kingdom.

units.zh: 壯大，通姦犯法，上以至親貰弗罪，傅相連坐。
units.en: Once grown, he fornicated and broke the law; the emperor spared him as kin, but his tutor and minister paid for it with their posts.
units.literal: When he grew to maturity he committed adultery and broke the law; the emperor, because he was closest kin, pardoned him without punishment, but the tutor and chancellor suffered joint liability.

units.zh: 久之，事太后，內不相得，太后上書言之，求守杜陵園。
units.en: In time he and the empress dowager fell out; she memorialized the throne and asked leave to retire to tend the Du imperial tombs.
units.literal: After a long time, in serving the empress dowager they were not harmonious within; the empress dowager submitted a memorial stating it and asked to guard the park at Du Mausoleum.

units.zh: 上於是遣太中大夫張子蟜奉璽書敕諭之，曰：「皇帝問東平王。
units.en: The emperor then sent Palace Grandee Zhang Zijiao with a sealed edict: “The Son of Heaven addresses the king of Dongping.
units.literal: The emperor thereupon sent Grand Counsellor of the Palace Zhang Zijiao bearing an imperial missive to admonish him, saying, “The emperor inquires of the King of Dongping.

units.zh: 蓋聞親親之恩莫重於孝，尊尊之義莫大於忠，故諸侯在位不驕以致孝道，制節謹度以冀天子，然後富貴不離於身，而社稷可保。
units.en: They say nothing binds kin like filial piety, nothing honors the throne like loyalty: a prince must curb pride to show filial duty, watch his bounds to await the emperor’s will—only then does fortune stay with him and the state remain secure.
units.literal: We have heard that in the kindness of cherishing kin nothing is weightier than filial piety, and in the duty of honoring the honored nothing is greater than loyalty; therefore the feudal kings in their positions do not act arrogantly so as to realize filial piety, restrain themselves and carefully keep measure so as to look to the Son of Heaven—then wealth and nobility do not leave their persons and the altars may be preserved.

units.zh: 今聞王自修有闕，本朝不和，流言紛紛，謗自內興，朕甚僭焉，為王懼之。
units.en: Word reaches me that your conduct has slipped, harmony with the court has failed, rumor runs wild, and slander rises under your own roof—I am deeply troubled and afraid for you.
units.literal: Now We hear the king’s self-cultivation has shortcomings, harmony with the capital is lacking, floating rumors swarm, slander arises from within—We are deeply distressed by this and fear for the king.

units.zh: 《詩》不雲乎？
units.en: Does not the Classic of Poetry say?
units.literal: Does not the Odes say?

units.zh: 『毋念爾祖，述修厥德，永言配命，自求多福』。
units.en: ‘Do not neglect your forebears; carry forward their virtue; ever match Heaven’s mandate; and seek blessing by your own deeds.’
units.literal: ‘Do not neglect your ancestors; pursue and cultivate their virtue; forever align with Heaven’s charge; seek much blessing for yourself.’

units.zh: 朕惟王之春秋方剛，忽於道德，意有所移，忠言未納，故臨遣太中大夫子蟜諭王朕意。
units.en: You are in the prime of life yet careless of virtue; you brush aside good counsel. I send Grandee Zijiao ahead of me to make my mind plain.
units.literal: We consider the king’s spring and autumn to be in full vigor, that he has neglected moral power, his intentions have shifted, loyal words have not been accepted—therefore on the verge of dispatch We send Grand Counsellor of the Palace Zijiao to declare to the king Our intention.

units.zh: 孔子曰：『過而不改，是謂過矣。』
units.en: Confucius said, ‘A fault uncorrected is a true fault.’
units.literal: Confucius said, ‘To err and not reform—that is what is called erring.’

units.zh: 王其深惟孰思之，無違朕意。」
units.en: Reflect long and hard, my cousin, and do not set yourself against my will.”
units.literal: Let the king ponder deeply and think it through; do not disobey Our intention.”

units.zh: 又特以璽書賜王太后，曰：「皇帝使諸吏宦者令承問東平王太后。
units.en: He also sent a personal edict to the king’s mother: “I charge the chief of household attendants to greet the queen mother of Dongping.
units.literal: In addition he specially with an imperial missive bestowed on the king’s mother, saying, “The emperor sends the Director of the Palace Attendants and Eunuchs to convey inquiry to the mother of the King of Dongping.

units.zh: 朕有聞，王太后少加意焉。
units.en: I have heard certain things; the queen mother should weigh them carefully.
units.literal: We have heard; let the king’s mother give a little attention.

units.zh: 夫福善之門莫美於和睦，患咎之首莫大於內離。
units.en: Nothing opens the door to blessing like concord at home; nothing breeds disaster like a split between mother and son.
units.literal: For the gate of blessing and goodness nothing is finer than harmony; for the head of calamity and fault nothing is greater than inner estrangement.

units.zh: 今東平王出襁褓之中而托於南面之位，以年齒方剛，涉學日寡，驁忽臣下，不自它於太后，以是之間，能無失禮義者，其唯聖人乎！
units.en: The King of Dongping came out of swaddling clothes and was entrusted with a south-facing throne. His age is just becoming vigorous, his study has been scant, he treats his ministers and officers arrogantly, and he does not humble himself before the empress dowager. In such circumstances, only a sage could avoid losing ritual and righteousness.
units.literal: Now the King of Dongping has come out of swaddling clothes and been entrusted with a south-facing seat; because his years and teeth are in full vigor, his study day by day is scant, he is proud and neglects ministers and officials, does not humble himself before the empress dowager—in such a gap, can one fail ritual and righteousness except the sage!

units.zh: 傳曰：『父為子隱，直在其中矣。』
units.en: The tradition runs, “A father shields a son’s faults, and therein lies justice.”
units.literal: The tradition says, “The father conceals for the son; uprightness is therein.”

units.zh: 王太后明察此意，不可不詳。
units.en: Queen mother, read this meaning clearly and leave no corner unexamined.
units.literal: The king’s mother should clearly examine this meaning; she cannot fail to be thorough.

units.zh: 閨門之內，母子之間，同氣異息，骨肉之恩，豈可忽哉！
units.en: Within the women’s quarters, between mother and child, one flesh and blood—how can you cast that bond aside?
units.literal: Within the inner gates, between mother and son, same breath yet different exhalations—the kindness of bone and flesh—how can it be neglected!

units.zh: 豈可忽哉！
units.en: You must not neglect it!
units.literal: How can it be neglected!

units.zh: 昔周公戒伯禽曰：『故舊無大故，則不可棄也，毋求備於一人。』
units.en: The Duke of Zhou warned Bo Qin: “Do not cast off old friends without grave cause; do not ask perfection of any single man.”
units.literal: In antiquity the Duke of Zhou admonished Bo Qin, saying, “Unless old associates have great fault, they must not be discarded; do not demand completeness in one person.”

units.zh: 夫以故舊之恩，猶忍小惡，而況此乎！
units.en: For old friends’ sake we forgive small slips—how much more between mother and son!
units.literal: By the kindness of old associates one still bears with small faults—how much more in this case!

units.zh: 已遣使者諭王，王既悔過服罪，太后寬忍以貰之，後宜不敢。
units.en: I have sent envoys to the king; he admits fault. Forgive him, madam, and he will not dare repeat it.
units.literal: We have already dispatched envoys to instruct the king; the king having repented faults and submitted to guilt, let the empress dowager be lenient and patient and pardon him; afterward he should not dare again.

units.zh: 王太后強餐，止思念，慎疾自愛。」
units.en: Eat for strength, madam, set worry aside, guard your health, and cherish yourself.”
units.literal: Let the king’s mother force herself to eat, stop anxious thoughts, be careful of illness and love herself.”

units.zh: 字慚俱，因使者頓首謝死罪，願灑心自改。
units.en: Yu was stricken with shame and fear; through the envoy he kowtowed for a capital crime and vowed to cleanse his heart and mend his ways.
units.literal: Yu was ashamed and afraid; through the envoy he knocked his head and begged pardon for a crime deserving death, wishing to cleanse his heart and reform himself.

units.zh: 詔書又敕傅相曰：「夫人之性皆有五常，及其少長，耳目牽於耆欲，故五常銷而邪心作，情亂其性，利勝其義，而不失厥家者，未之有也。
units.en: Another edict told tutor and minister: “Every man is born with the five constant virtues, yet age and appetite pull him off course until desire corrupts nature and gain drowns duty—none who so drift keep their house intact.
units.literal: An edict again instructed the tutor and chancellor, saying, “In human nature all have the five constants; when they grow from youth to adulthood, ears and eyes are pulled by fond desires, therefore the five constants wear away and wicked hearts arise, emotion disorders nature, profit overcomes righteousness—and yet not to lose one’s house: there has never been such a case.

units.zh: 今王富於春秋，氣力勇武，獲師傅之教淺，加以少所聞見，自今以來，非《五經》之正術，敢以遊獵非禮道王者，輒以名聞。」
units.en: The king is young, strong, and lightly taught, with narrow experience. Henceforth, if anyone leads him hunting or down unorthodox paths outside the Five Classics, report that man’s name at once.”
units.literal: Now the king is rich in spring and autumn, his vigor is brave and martial, what he has received from tutor and teacher is shallow, and in addition he has heard and seen little; from now on, whoever dares to lead the king in hunting excursions by ways not of ritual that are not the orthodox arts of the Five Classics, immediately report the name.”

units.zh: 宇立二十年，元帝崩。
units.en: Twenty years after Yu took the throne, Yuan died.
units.literal: Yu had been established twenty years when Emperor Yuan died.

units.zh: 宇謂中謁者信等曰：「漢大臣議天子少弱，未能治天下，以為我知文法，建欲使我輔佐天子。
units.en: Yu told the usher Xin and others, “The great ministers think the boy emperor too weak to rule and, because I know the statutes, mean to set me at his elbow.
units.literal: Yu said to the palace usher Xin and others, “Han ministers have deliberated that the Son of Heaven is young and weak and unable to govern the realm; they consider that I understand statutes and precedents, and propose that I assist the Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 我見尚書晨夜極苦，使我為之，不能也。
units.en: I have watched the masters of writing toil day and night—I could never bear that office.
units.literal: I have seen how the secretariat works morning and night in extreme toil; were it made me to do it, I could not.

units.zh: 今暑熱，縣官年少，持服恐無處所，我危得之！」
units.en: The weather is stifling, the emperor is young, and when the court goes into mourning it may have no pillar to lean on—I could nearly win the post!”
units.literal: Now it is hot; the Son of Heaven is young; when he dons mourning I fear the court will have nowhere to turn—I could nearly obtain it!”

units.zh: 比至下，宇凡三哭，飲酒食肉，妻妾不離側。
units.en: When the edict of mourning arrived, Yu wept three times for show, then feasted on wine and meat while his wives and concubines never left his side.
units.literal: By the time the mourning edict came down, Yu had wept only three times in all, drank wine and ate meat, and wives and concubines did not leave his side.

units.zh: 又姬朐臑故親幸，後疏遠，數歎息呼天。
units.en: A former favorite, the concubine Qu Nai, had been cast aside; she sighed to heaven again and again.
units.literal: Also his concubine Qu Nai had formerly been favored; afterward she was estranged and several times sighed and called to Heaven.

units.zh: 宇聞，斥朐臑為家人子，掃除永巷，數笞擊之。
units.en: Yu heard it, reduced her to menial rank, put her to sweeping the palace lane, and beat her repeatedly.
units.literal: When Yu heard, he demoted Qu Nai to the rank of family servant, set her to sweeping the long lane, and several times flogged her.

units.zh: 朐臑私疏宇過失，數令家告之。
units.en: She drafted a secret catalogue of his misdeeds and had kin report them upstream.
units.literal: Qu Nai privately drafted a list of Yu’s faults and several times had her family report them.

units.zh: 宇覺知，絞殺朐臑。
units.en: When Yu found out, he strangled her.
units.literal: When Yu perceived it, he strangled Qu Nai to death.

units.zh: 有司奏請逮捕，有詔削樊、亢父二縣。
units.en: Officials asked for his arrest; the emperor instead stripped two counties—Fan and Kangfu—from his fief.
units.literal: The responsible officials memorialized requesting arrest; there was an edict stripping Fan and Kangfu, two counties.

units.zh: 後三歲，天子詔有司曰：「蓋聞仁以親親，古之道也。
units.en: Three years later the emperor told his officers: “Kindness begins with kin—that was the way of the ancients.
units.literal: After three years the Son of Heaven ordered the responsible officials, saying, “We have heard that benevolence lies in cherishing kin—this is the way of antiquity.

units.zh: 前東平王有闕，有司請廢，朕不忍。
units.en: When Dongping erred before, some urged me to depose him; I could not.
units.literal: Formerly the King of Dongping had faults; the responsible officials asked to depose him; We could not bear it.

units.zh: 又請削，朕不敢專。
units.en: Others asked to shave his domain; I would not act unilaterally.
units.literal: They again asked to strip territory; We did not dare decide alone.

units.zh: 惟王之至親，未嘗忘於心。
units.en: Yet you are bone of my bone—I have not forgotten you.
units.literal: Only as to the king’s closest kin, We have never forgotten it in Our heart.

units.zh: 今聞王改行自新，尊修經術，親近仁人，非法之求，不以奸吏，朕甚嘉焉。
units.en: Word comes that you have mended your ways, take the classics seriously, keep company with good men, and no longer let sharp clerks peddle illicit favors—I applaud that.
units.literal: Now We hear the king has changed conduct and renewed himself, honors and cultivates the classics, draws near to benevolent men, and does not employ crafty clerks for unlawful requests—We greatly approve.

units.zh: 傳不雲乎？
units.en: Does not the tradition say?
units.literal: Does not the tradition say?

units.zh: 朝過夕改，君子與之。
units.en: Wrong at dawn and right by dusk wins the gentleman’s praise.
units.literal: Fault in the morning and reform by evening—the gentleman approves.

units.zh: 其復前所削縣如故。」
units.en: Restore the counties I once took away.”
units.literal: Let him restore the former stripped counties as before.”

units.zh: 後年來朝，上疏求諸子及《太史公書》，上以問大將軍王鳳，對曰：「臣聞諸侯朝聘，考文章，正法度，非禮不言。
units.en: The following year he attended court and asked for the Masters compendia and Sima Qian’s history. The emperor consulted Wang Feng, who answered, “When kings come to audience they are to polish their style and law, not to chatter outside ritual.
units.literal: The next year he came to court and submitted a memorial requesting the Masters texts and the Grand Scribe’s Records; the emperor thereupon asked Grand General Wang Feng, who replied, “Your subject has heard that when feudal kings attend court they examine literary patterns and correct standards of law; they do not speak what is not ritual.

units.zh: 今東平王幸得來朝，不思制節謹度，以防危失，而求諸書，非朝聘之義也。
units.en: Dongping should be tightening his belt, not courting danger by begging for books—that is not what a court visit is for.
units.literal: Now the King of Dongping has been fortunate enough to come to court yet does not think of restraining himself and carefully keeping measure to guard against danger and loss, but seeks books—this is not the meaning of court attendance.

units.zh: 諸子書或反經術，非聖人；
units.en: Some of those miscellanies subvert the classics and fall short of the sages;
units.literal: Among the Masters texts some oppose the classics and are not sages;

units.zh: 或明鬼神，信物怪；
units.en: others retail ghosts, omens, and the uncanny;
units.literal: some make clear ghosts and spirits and trust in prodigies;

units.zh: 《太史公書》有戰國縱橫權譎之謀，漢興之初謀臣奇策，天官災異，地形厄塞：皆不宜在諸侯王。
units.en: The Grand Scribe’s Records contains the vertical-and-horizontal stratagems and cunning plans of the Warring States, the strange plans of advisers at the beginning of Han’s rise, celestial offices and disaster anomalies, and terrain with strategic passes and choke points; none of these are suitable for a feudal king to possess.
units.literal: the Grand Scribe’s Records has Warring States vertical-and-horizontal cunning stratagems, strange plans of founding ministers at the rise of Han, celestial offices and disaster anomalies, terrain with narrow passes: all are unsuitable for feudal kings.

units.zh: 不可予。
units.en: They must not be granted.
units.literal: They must not be granted.

units.zh: 不許之辭宜曰：『《五經》聖人所制，萬事靡不畢載。
units.en: Your refusal should read: ‘The Five Classics, fashioned by the sages, hold everything worth knowing.
units.literal: The wording of refusal should say, ‘The Five Classics were made by sages; myriad affairs are therein fully recorded.

units.zh: 王審樂道，傅相皆儒者，旦夕講誦，足以正身虞意。
units.en: If my cousin loves the Way, his tutors are Ru scholars who can drill him dawn to dusk until mind and conduct are straight.
units.literal: If the king examines and delights in the Way, tutor and chancellor are all Confucians; morning and evening they lecture and recite—enough to correct the body and settle the mind.

units.zh: 夫小辯破義，小道不通，致遠恐泥，皆不足以留意。
units.en: Small cleverness breaks the great pattern; side paths lead nowhere—fixing on them only mires the traveler.
units.literal: Petty disputation breaks righteousness, petty paths do not reach far—to go far one fears miring; all are insufficient to fix attention on.

units.zh: 諸益於經術者，不愛於王。』」
units.en: Whatever serves the classics, I do not withhold from you.’”
units.literal: Whatever benefits the classics and techniques, We do not begrudge the king.’”

units.zh: 對奏，天子如鳳言，遂不與。
units.en: The emperor accepted Feng’s memorial and denied the books.
units.literal: When the reply was memorialized, the Son of Heaven followed Feng’s words and therefore did not grant them.

units.zh: 立三十三年薨，子煬王雲嗣。
units.en: He reigned thirty-three years and died; his son Yun, posthumously Yang, succeeded.
units.literal: He was established thirty-three years and died; his son King Yang Yun succeeded.

units.zh: 哀帝時，無鹽危山土自起覆草，如馳道狀，又瓠山石轉立。
units.en: In Emperor Ai’s reign soil at Wuyan’s Danger Mountain heaved up over the turf in the shape of an imperial causeway, and a boulder at Gourd Mountain rolled upright.
units.literal: Under Emperor Ai, at Danger Mountain in Wuyan earth rose of itself and covered grass in the shape of an imperial thoroughfare; also at Gourd Mountain a stone turned and stood upright.

units.zh: 雲及後謁自之石所祭，治石像瓠山立石，束倍草，並祠之。
units.en: Yun and Queen Ye visited the omens, set up a stone like the one at Gourd Mountain, bound paired stalks of grass, and offered joint sacrifice.
units.literal: Yun and his queen Ye went in person to the stone place to sacrifice, worked a stone in the image of the Gourd Mountain standing stone, tied double grass, and jointly sacrificed to them.

units.zh: 建平三年，息夫躬、孫寵等共因幸臣董賢告之。
units.en: In Jianping 3, Xi Fu Gong, Sun Chong, and others denounced them through the favorite Dong Xian.
units.literal: In the third year of Jianping, Xi Fu Gong, Sun Chong, and others together through the favored minister Dong Xian reported it.

units.zh: 是時，哀帝被疾，多所惡，事下有司，逮王、後謁下獄驗治，言使巫傅恭、婢合歡等祠祭詛祝上，為雲求為天子。
units.en: Ai was ill and ill-tempered; officers jailed king and queen and proved they had set shamans Fu Gong and the slave girl Hehuan cursing the throne so Yun might become Son of Heaven.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Ai was afflicted with illness and had many taboos; the matter was handed to the responsible officials, who arrested the king and Queen Ye and put them in prison for examination; it was said they had shamans Fu Gong and the maid Hehuan and others sacrifice and curse-pray for the emperor, seeking the kingship for Yun.

units.zh: 雲又與知災異者高尚等指星宿，言上疾必不愈，雲當得天下。
units.en: Yun and omen-readers such as Gao Shang traced the stars, swearing the emperor would not recover and the mandate would fall to Yun.
units.literal: Yun also with one who knew disasters and anomalies, Gao Shang and others, pointed to asterisms, saying the emperor’s illness would surely not improve and Yun ought to obtain the realm.

units.zh: 石立，宣帝起之表也。
units.en: The standing stone had been the omen of Emperor Xuan’s ascent.
units.literal: The stone standing upright was the sign of Emperor Xuan’s rise.

units.zh: 有司請誅王，有詔廢徙房陵。
units.en: Some demanded the king’s death; the edict spared his life but deposed him and banished him to Fangling.
units.literal: The responsible officials asked to execute the king; there was an edict deposing him and moving him to Fangling.

units.zh: 雲自殺，謁棄市。
units.en: Yun committed suicide; Ye was executed in the marketplace.
units.literal: Yun killed himself; Ye was exposed in the market.

units.zh: 立十七年，國除。
units.en: Seventeen years into his reign the kingdom was abolished.
units.literal: He had been established seventeen years; the state was abolished.

units.zh: 元始元年，王莽欲反哀帝政，白太皇太后，立雲太子開明為東平王，又立思王孫成都為中山王。
units.en: In Yuanshi 1, Wang Mang, undoing Ai’s policies, persuaded the grand empress dowager to make Yun’s heir Kai Ming king of Dongping and to enfeoff Chengdu, grandson of the Prince of Dongping, as king of Zhongshan.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanshi, Wang Mang wished to reverse Emperor Ai’s policies, reported to the Grand Empress Dowager, established Kai Ming, heir of Yun, as King of Dongping, and also established Chengdu, grandson of Prince Si, as King of Zhongshan.

units.zh: 開明立三年，薨，無子。
units.en: Kai Ming reigned three years and died without issue.
units.literal: Kai Ming was established three years and died; he had no son.

units.zh: 復立開明兄嚴鄉侯信子匡為東平王，奉開明後。
units.en: The court then set Kuang, son of Marquis Yanxiang Xin, on the Dongping throne to continue Kai Ming’s line.
units.literal: They again established Kuang, son of Marquis Yanxiang Xin, as King of Dongping, to continue Kai Ming’s line.

units.zh: 王莽居攝，東郡太守翟義與嚴鄉侯信謀舉兵誅莽，立信為天子。
units.en: Under Mang’s regency the eastern governor Zhai Yi conspired with Marquis Xin to march against Mang and proclaimed Xin emperor.
units.literal: When Wang Mang held regency, Governor of the Eastern Region Zhai Yi plotted with Marquis Yanxiang Xin to raise troops to execute Mang and established Xin as Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 兵敗，皆為莽所滅。
units.en: Their forces were crushed and Mang wiped them out.
units.literal: The army was defeated; all were destroyed by Mang.

units.zh: 中山哀王竟
units.en: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing
units.literal: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing

units.zh: 中山哀王竟，初元二年立為清河王。
units.en: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing, was made king of Qinghe in Chuyuan 2.
units.literal: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing, in the second year of Chuyuan was established as King of Qinghe.

units.zh: 三年，徙中山，以幼少未之國。
units.en: The next year he was transferred to Zhongshan but, still a child, did not take up the fief.
units.literal: In the third year he was moved to Zhongshan; because he was young and small he did not go to the kingdom.

units.zh: 建昭四年，薨邸，葬杜陵，無子，絕。
units.en: He died at the princely residence in Jianzhao 4 and was buried at Du; without an heir the line ended.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhao he died in the lodge, was buried at Du Mausoleum, had no son, and the line was cut off.

units.zh: 太后歸居外家戎氏。
units.en: His mother the queen dowager went back to live with her Rong kin.
units.literal: The empress dowager returned to dwell with her maternal Rong clan.

units.zh: 孝元皇帝三男
units.en: Emperor Yuan had three sons
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons

units.zh: 孝元皇帝三男。
units.en: Emperor Yuan had three sons.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons.

units.zh: 王皇后生孝成帝，傅昭儀生定陶共王康，馮昭儀生中山孝王興。
units.en: Empress Wang gave birth to Emperor Cheng. Lady Fu the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang; Lady Feng the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing.
units.literal: Empress Wang bore Emperor Xiaocheng; Lady Fu the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang; Lady Feng the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing.

units.zh: 定陶共王康
units.en: Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang
units.literal: Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang

units.zh: 定陶共王康，永光三年立為濟陽王。
units.en: Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang, was enfeoffed as king of Jiyang in the third year of Yongguang.
units.literal: Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang, in the third year of Yongguang was established as King of Jiyang.

units.zh: 八年，徙為山陽王。
units.en: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shanyang.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was moved to be King of Shanyang.

units.zh: 八年，徙定陶。
units.en: He was then transferred to Dingtao.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was moved to Dingtao.

units.zh: 王少而愛，長多材藝，習知音聲，上奇器之。
units.en: The emperor doted on him from boyhood; grown, he was versatile and musical, and the throne marked him as exceptional.
units.literal: The king from youth was loved; grown, he had many talents and arts, was practiced in knowing music and sounds, and the emperor regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 母昭儀又幸，幾代皇后太子。
units.en: His mother the brilliant companion was also favored and several times nearly unseated empress and crown prince.
units.literal: The mother Brilliant Companion was also favored and several times nearly replaced the empress and heir.

units.zh: 語在《元后》及《史丹傳》。
units.en: The story is told in the biographies of Empress Yuan and Shi Dan.
units.literal: The account is in the “Empress Yuan” and “Shi Dan” biographies.

units.zh: 成帝即位，緣先帝意，厚遇異於它王。
units.en: When Cheng succeeded, he followed his predecessor's wishes and favored him more generously than any other prince.
units.literal: When Emperor Cheng took the throne, following the former emperor's intent, he treated him generously, differently from other kings.

units.zh: 十九年薨，子欣嗣。
units.en: He died in the nineteenth year of his reign; his son Xin inherited.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; his son Xin succeeded.

units.zh: 十五年，成帝無子，徵入為皇太子。
units.en: In the fifteenth year of Xin's reign, as Emperor Cheng had no son, Xin was summoned to the capital as crown prince.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year, as Emperor Cheng had no son, Xin was summoned to enter the capital as heir apparent.

units.zh: 上以太子奉大宗後，不得顧私親，乃立楚思王子景為定陶王，奉共王後。
units.en: Because the crown prince was to carry on the main imperial line and could not favor his own kin, the emperor made Jing, son of Prince Si of Chu, king of Dingtao to continue Prince Gong's line.
units.literal: The emperor, because the heir apparent was to serve the main lineage and could not attend to private kin, thereupon established Jing, son of Prince Si of Chu, as King of Dingtao to continue the line of Prince Gong.

units.zh: 成帝崩，太子即位，是為孝哀帝。
units.en: When Emperor Cheng died, the crown prince ascended as Emperor Ai.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng died; the heir apparent took the throne—this was Emperor Ai.

units.zh: 即位二年，追尊共王為共皇帝，置寢廟京師，序昭穆，儀如孝元帝。
units.en: In the second year of his reign he posthumously honored Prince Gong as Emperor Gong, set up his spirit temple in the capital, arranged the zhao and mu order, and followed the ceremonial model of Emperor Xiaoyuan.
units.literal: In the second year of his reign he posthumously honored Prince Gong as Emperor Gong, established his spirit temple in the capital, arranged the ancestral order of zhao and mu, with ceremonies like those for Emperor Xiaoyuan.

units.zh: 徙定陶王景為信都王云。
units.en: King Jing of Dingtao was transferred to Xindu, the record says.
units.literal: Jing was moved from King of Dingtao to King of Xindu, it is said.

units.zh: 中山孝王興
units.en: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing
units.literal: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing

units.zh: 中山孝王興，建昭二年立為信都王。
units.en: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing, was made king of Xindu in Jianzhao 2.
units.literal: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing, in the second year of Jianzhao was established as King of Xindu.

units.zh: 十四年，徙中山。
units.en: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Zhongshan.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he was moved to Zhongshan.

units.zh: 成帝之議立太子也，御史大夫孔光以為《尚書》有殷及王，兄終弟及，中山王元帝之子，宜為後。
units.en: When Cheng debated the succession, Imperial Counselor Kong Guang cited the Documents on Yin brother-to-brother transmission and argued that Xing, Yuan’s son and king of Zhongshan, should follow.
units.literal: When Emperor Cheng deliberated establishing the heir apparent, Imperial Counselor Kong Guang thought the Documents had Yin and royal houses where the elder brother ended and the younger brother succeeded; the King of Zhongshan was Emperor Yuan’s son and ought to be successor.

units.zh: 成帝以中山王不材，又兄弟，不得相入廟。
units.en: Cheng judged Xing unfit and held that brothers could not share one temple line.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng considered the King of Zhongshan untalented and also that brothers could not enter one another’s temples.

units.zh: 外家王氏與趙昭儀皆欲用哀帝為太子，故遂立焉。
units.en: The Wangs at court and Lady Zhao the brilliant companion both wanted Ai as heir, so he was chosen.
units.literal: The maternal Wang clan and Lady Zhao the Brilliant Companion both wished to use Emperor Ai as heir apparent; therefore he was finally established.

units.zh: 上乃封孝王舅馮參為宜鄉侯，而益封孝王萬戶，以尉其意。
units.en: The emperor then made Xing’s uncle Feng Can marquis of Yixiang and added ten thousand households to Xing’s fief to soothe him.
units.literal: The emperor thereupon enfeoffed Prince Xiao’s maternal uncle Feng Can as Marquis of Yixiang and increased Prince Xiao’s fief by ten thousand households to comfort his mind.

units.zh: 三十年，薨，子衎嗣。
units.en: He died in the thirtieth year of his reign; his son Kan inherited.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year he died; his son Kan succeeded.

units.zh: 七年，哀帝崩，無子，征中山王衎入即位，是為平帝。
units.en: In the seventh year of Kan’s reign Ai died childless; Kan was summoned to the capital as Emperor Ping.
units.literal: In the seventh year Emperor Ai died without a son; they summoned the King of Zhongshan Kan to enter and take the throne—this was Emperor Ping.

units.zh: 太皇太后以帝為成帝後，故立東平思王孫桃鄉頃侯子成都為中山王，奉孝王後。
units.en: The grand empress dowager, treating Ping as Cheng’s heir, enfeoffed Chengdu—son of Marquis Qing of Taoxiang and grandson of Prince Si of Dongping—as king of Zhongshan to carry on Xing’s line.
units.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager, because the emperor was to continue Cheng’s line, therefore established Chengdu, son of Marquis Qing of Taoxiang, grandson of Prince Si of Dongping, as King of Zhongshan, to continue Prince Xiao’s line.

units.zh: 王莽時絕。
units.en: The line ended under Wang Mang.
units.literal: At the time of Wang Mang the line was cut off.

units.zh: 贊曰：孝元之後，遍有天下，然而世絕於孫，豈非天哉！
units.en: The summation runs: from Emperor Yuan onward they held all under heaven, yet the line died with the grandson—can we call it anything but fate?
units.literal: The eulogy says: After Emperor Xiaoyuan, they broadly held the realm, yet the generations were cut off at the grandson—is it not Heaven!

units.zh: 淮陽憲王於時諸侯為聰察矣，張博誘之，幾陷無道。
units.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was the sharpest of the kings of his day; Zhang Bo led him to the brink of treason.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was among the feudal lords the most perceptive; Zhang Bo enticed him and he nearly fell into lack of the Way.

units.zh: 《詩》云「貪人敗類」，古今一也。
units.en: The Classic of Poetry says, “The greedy man destroys his kind”—the same in ancient times and today.
units.literal: The Odes says, “The greedy man destroys his kind”—the same in ancient times and today.

units.zh: 太子曰：「顏子縮屋稱貞，柳下嫗而不亂，未若此翁白首不娶者也。」
units.en: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui was praised for chastity though he lived in a hovel, and Liu Xiahui kept his integrity though he shared a blanket with a woman—but neither can match this old man who has never married even to white hair."
units.literal: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui, who shrank in his hut, was called chaste; Liu Xiahui, who shared a blanket with a woman, was not corrupted—yet neither equals this old man, white-haired and never married."

units.zh: 曲陽侯根前為三公輔政，知趙昭儀殺皇子，不輒白奏，反與趙氏比周，恣意妄行，譖訴故許後，被加以非罪，誅破諸許族，敗元帝外家。
units.en: Wang Gen, marquis of Quyang, had served among the Three Excellencies and helped direct the government. He knew that Consort Zhao Hede had killed the imperial sons but failed to report it. Instead he colluded with the Zhao clan, acted without restraint, slandered the deposed Empress Xu, had her falsely condemned, destroyed the Xu clan, and ruined Emperor Yuan's maternal family.
units.literal: Marquis of Quyang Wang Gen had earlier assisted the government as one of the Three Excellencies. He knew that Consort Zhao Hede had killed the imperial sons but did not immediately report it; instead he allied himself with the Zhao clan, acted willfully and recklessly, slandered the deposed Empress Xu, imposed false charges on her, destroyed the Xu clan, and ruined Emperor Yuan's maternal family.

units.zh: 六月甲辰，丞相玄成薨。
units.en: On Jiachen of the sixth month, Chancellor Xuancheng passed away.
units.literal: Sixth month Jiachen, Chancellor Xuancheng passed away.

units.zh: 是歲，御史大夫王駿卒。
units.en: In this year, Imperial Secretary Grandee Wang Jun passed away.
units.literal: This year, Imperial Secretary Grandee Wang Jun passed away.

units.zh: 譬若以周、邵為丞相，孔丘為御史大夫，太公為將軍，畢公高拾遺於後，弁嚴子為衛尉，皋陶為大理，後稷為司農，伊尹為少府，子贛使外國，顏、閔為博士，子夏為太常，益為右扶風，季路為執金吾，契為鴻臚，龍逢為宗正，伯夷為京兆，管仲為馮翊，魯般為將作，仲山甫為光祿，申伯為太僕，延陵季子為水衡，百里奚為典屬國，柳下惠為大長秋，史魚為司直，蘧伯玉為太傅，孔父為詹事，孫叔敖為諸侯相，子產為郡守，王慶忌為期門，夏育為鼎官，羿為旄頭，宋萬為式道候。」
units.en: Imagine the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao as your chancellors; Confucius as chief censor; the Grand Duke as commander; Duke Bi Gao as court remonstrant; Bian Zhuangzi as captain of the guard; Gao Yao as chief judge; Hou Ji as minister of agriculture; Yi Yin as palace treasurer; Zigong as foreign envoy; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian as court scholars; Zixia as master of rites; Yi as western capital intendant; Zilu as capital commandant; Xie as master of guest ceremonies; Guan Longpeng as keeper of the imperial genealogy; the minister Boyi as metropolitan governor; Guan Zhong as northern capital intendant; Lu Ban as chief engineer; Zhong Shanfu as palace chamberlain; the Earl of Shen as master of the horse; Prince Jizi of Yanling as keeper of parks and waters; Baili Xi as commissioner for dependent peoples; Liuxia Hui as chamberlain to the empress; Shi Yu as censor of conduct; Qu Boyu as grand tutor; Kong Fu as supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao as chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan as commandery governor; Prince Qingji as a palace gate guard; Xia Yu as cauldron officer; Yi the Archer as vanguard officer; and Song Wan as road-clearing scout."
units.literal: It is as if you had made the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao your chancellors; Confucius your Censor-in-Chief; the Grand Duke your general; Duke Bi Gao your remonstrant at the rear; Bian Zhuangzi your Commandant of the Guards; Gao Yao your Chief Justice; Hou Ji your Minister of Agriculture; Yi Yin your Privy Treasurer; Zigong your envoy abroad; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian your Erudites; Zixia your Minister of Ceremonies; Yi your western capital intendant; Zilu your Capital Commandant; Xie your Grand Herald; Guan Longpeng your Director of the Imperial Clan; the minister Boyi your Metropolitan Governor; Guan Zhong your northern capital intendant; Lu Ban your Superintendent of Works; Zhong Shanfu your Chamberlain for Attendants; the Earl of Shen your Grand Coachman; Prince Jizi of Yanling your Superintendent of Waters and Parks; Baili Xi your Director of Dependent States; Liuxia Hui your Chamberlain for the Empress; Shi Yu your Rectifier; Qu Boyu your Grand Tutor; Kong Fu your supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao your chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan your commandery governor; Prince Qingji your Palace Gate Guard; Xia Yu your Cauldron Officer; Yi the Archer your Vanguard Officer; and Song Wan your road-clearing scout."

units.zh: 立弟竟為清河王。
units.en: Established younger brother Jing as King of Qinghe.
units.literal: Established younger brother Jing as Qinghe King.

units.zh: 六月甲申，中山王竟薨。
units.en: On Jiashen of the sixth month, King Jing of Zhongshan passed away.
units.literal: Sixth month Jiashen, Zhongshan King Jing passed away.

units.zh: 二年春正月，行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。
units.en: In the first month of spring in the second year, His Majesty proceeded to Ganquan and performed the suburban sacrifice at the Supreme Altar.
units.literal: Second year spring first month, proceeded favored Ganquan, suburban Supreme Altar.

units.zh: 封中山王舅諫大夫馮參為宜鄉侯，益中山國三萬戶，以慰其意。
units.en: Enfeoffed Zhongshan King's maternal uncle Remonstrance Grandee Feng Can as Marquis of Yixiang, increased the Zhongshan kingdom by 30,000 households, to console his intention.
units.literal: Enfeoffed Zhongshan King maternal uncle Remonstrance Grandee Feng Can as Yixiang Marquis, increased Zhongshan kingdom 30,000 households, to console his intention.

units.zh: 於是韋賢以老病免，相遂代為丞相，封高平侯，食邑八百戶。
units.en: Wei Xian was then dismissed on account of old age and illness, and Wei Xiang succeeded him as chancellor, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoping with eight hundred households.
units.literal: Thereupon Wei Xian was dismissed on account of old age and illness, and Xiang then replaced him as chancellor, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoping, with a fief of eight hundred households.

units.zh: 孝哀皇帝，元帝庶孫，定陶恭王子也。
units.en: Emperor Ai was a grandson of Emperor Yuan through a concubine, and the son of Prince Gong of Dingtao.
units.literal: Emperor Ai (posthumous title Filial-Lamenting) was a grandson of Emperor Yuan through a concubine, and the son of Prince Gong of Dingtao.

units.zh: 贊曰：孝哀自為藩王及充太子之宮，文辭博敏，幼有令聞。
units.en: Appraisal: Emperor Ai, from his time as a feudal king to his tenure as Crown Prince, displayed extensive and nimble literary skills, earning an excellent reputation from his youth.
units.literal: Appraisal says: Filial and Lamented, from being a feudal king and filling the position of Crown Prince, had broad and quick literary compositions, from youth had excellent reputation.

units.zh: 上怪之，以問定陶王，對曰：「令，諸侯王朝，得從其國二千石。
units.en: The emperor found this strange and asked the King of Dingtao about it. He replied: 'According to the regulations, when feudal lords come to court, they are allowed to bring officials ranked at two thousand bushels from their domains.
units.literal: The emperor was surprised by this and asked the King of Dingtao about it. He replied: 'According to the regulations, when feudal lords come to court, they may bring officials of two thousand bushels from their fiefs.

units.zh: 成帝由此以為不能，而賢定陶王，數稱其材。
units.en: From this, Emperor Cheng concluded that the King of Zhongshan was incompetent, but he came to admire the King of Dingtao and often praised his talents.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng thereby considered the King of Zhongshan incapable, but esteemed the King of Dingtao and frequently praised his abilities.

units.zh: 明年，使執金吾任宏守大鴻臚，持節徵定陶王，立為皇太子。
units.en: The following year, Emperor Cheng sent Colonel Ren Hong, temporarily serving as Grand Herald, to summon the King of Dingtao with imperial credentials and establish him as Crown Prince.
units.literal: The next year, he sent Colonel of the City Gates Ren Hong, acting as Grand Herald, bearing credentials to summon the King of Dingtao and establish him as Crown Prince.

units.zh: 四月丙午，太子即皇帝位，謁高廟。
units.en: In the fourth month, on the day bingwu, the Crown Prince ascended the throne as emperor and performed the ancestral rites at the imperial temple.
units.literal: In the fourth month, on the day Bingwu, the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne and paid respects at the High Temple.

units.zh: 號曰陳聖劉太平皇帝。
units.en: The title shall be Emperor Taiping of the Chengsheng Liu.
units.literal: The title shall be Emperor Taiping of the Chengsheng Liu.

units.zh: 六月戊午，帝崩于未央宮。
units.en: In the sixth month, on the day wuwu, the emperor died in the Weiyang Palace.
units.literal: In the sixth month, on the day wuwu, the emperor passed away in the Weiyang Palace.

units.zh: 五月丙戌，立皇后傅氏。
units.en: In the fifth month, on the day bingxu, he installed Lady Fu as empress.
units.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Bingxu, he established Empress Fu.

units.zh: 元延四年入朝，盡從傅、相、中尉。
units.en: In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (9 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyan, he came to court, his tutor, chancellor, and commandant all accompanying him.

units.zh: 綏和二年三月，成帝崩。
units.en: In the third month of the second year of the Suihe era (7 BCE), Emperor Cheng died.
units.literal: In the third month of the second year of Suihe, Emperor Cheng passed away.

units.zh: 建平元年春正月，赦天下。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the first year of the Jianping era (6 BCE), a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Jianping, he granted amnesty to all under heaven.

units.zh: 二年春三月，罷大司空，復御史大夫。
units.en: In the third month of spring of the second year, the office of Grand Minister of Works was abolished and the Censor-in-Chief was restored.
units.literal: In the third month of spring of the second year, he abolished the Grand Minister of Works and restored the Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 侍詔夏賀良等言赤精子之讖，漢家曆運中衰，當再受命，宜改元易號。
units.en: Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others cited the prophecy of the Red Essence Child, saying that the Han dynasty's ordained fortune was in decline and should receive the Mandate anew, and that the era name and imperial title ought to be changed.
units.literal: Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others spoke of the prophecy of the Red Essence Child: the Han house's ordained fortune was in mid-decline and should receive the Mandate anew; the era name and imperial title ought to be changed.

units.zh: 以建平二年為太初元將元年。
units.en: Let the second year of Jianping be the first year of Taichu Yuanjiang.
units.literal: Let the second year of Jianping be the first year of Taichu Yuanjiang.

units.zh: 三年春正月，立廣德夷王弟廣漢為廣平王。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the third year, King Yi of Guangde's younger brother Guanghan was installed as King of Guangping.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year, he established King Yi of Guangde's younger brother Guanghan as King of Guangping.

units.zh: 四年春，大旱。
units.en: In the spring of the fourth year, a severe drought occurred.
units.literal: In spring of the fourth year, great drought.

units.zh: 二月，封帝太太后從弟侍中傅商為汝昌侯，太后同母弟子侍中鄭業為陽信侯。
units.en: In the second month, the emperor enfeoffed the Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin, Chamberlain Fu Shang, as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's younger uterine brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.
units.literal: In the second month, he enfeoffed Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin Chamberlain Fu Shang as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.

units.zh: 元壽元年春正月辛丑朔，日有蝕之。
